title: Best Tax Prep Service 2026: In-Person, Online & Free Options
description: Compare H&R Block, Jackson Hewitt, TurboTax Live, local CPA, and VITA free filing. Costs, audit support, and who each service actually fits.
lede: The price differences ranged from $0 to $1,100. This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews
methodology: Each service is compared on published pricing for a moderately complex return (Schedule C + Schedule E + two state returns), the audit support terms in each provider's agreement, stated availability for reaching a preparer, and the accuracy and refund guarantees each company publishes.

sections.heading: How we compared: the four things that actually matter
paragraphs: Most tax prep comparisons stop at base price. That misses the real cost. A $99 online tier can balloon to $350 once you add state returns, Schedule C, and a rental property. Every service here is priced from published rate cards against one fixed scenario: $62,000 in W-2 income, $18,000 in freelance income (Schedule C), one rental property (Schedule E), and filings in California plus Nevada.

The comparison therefore uses all-in cost — federal, each state return, and every paid add-on — rather than the advertised entry price. A service that costs $200 more but surfaces $400 in overlooked deductions is still the better deal.

| Service | Price range | Key strength | Audit support | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H&R Block In-Person | $80–$300 | 9,000 offices, walk-in access | Included | Best overall in-person |
| Jackson Hewitt | $75–$250 | Flat-fee pricing, Walmart kiosks | Lifetime Guarantee | Best for predictable cost |
| TurboTax Live Full Service | $89–$469 | Expert handles everything online | Included | Best online experience |
| Local CPA / EA | $300–$1,500+ | Highest expertise, year-round advice | Varies | Best for truly complex returns |
| IRS VITA (free) | $0 | IRS-certified, no upsells | Not offered | Best if income under $67K |

sections.heading: H&R Block In-Person — best for walk-in convenience
paragraphs: H&R Block has 9,000 US offices, more than any national chain. Walk-in availability from late January through April 15 means no appointment needed for straightforward returns. For this scenario, published rates put the in-person all-in price around $185 for federal plus California, with Nevada as a same-day add-on for about $45. Total: $230.

The preparers hold the company's own certification, which requires 80+ hours of training plus annual updates. That is not the same as a CPA, but it is more than a seasonal hire doing a three-day course. The Accuracy Guarantee covers penalties and interest caused by H&R Block errors — audit representation is included at no extra charge through their Peace of Mind plan (automatically applied in most offices).

The variable no comparison can control: preparer quality differs by location. Offices in high-traffic urban areas tend to have more experienced staff. Customer reports describe the same gap repeatedly — a home-office deduction raised during the interview that never made it onto the finished return, for example. The company's nationwide training is good; individual execution is uneven. If your return is genuinely complex, ask up front whether the local office has a preparer who handles Schedule E regularly.

sections.heading: Jackson Hewitt — best for flat-fee predictability
paragraphs: Jackson Hewitt's main differentiator is flat-fee pricing. You pay one price regardless of which schedules your return requires. For this scenario the flat price is about $219 — federal, two states, Schedule C, Schedule E, all included. H&R Block would come to about $230 on the same inputs, so Jackson Hewitt lands slightly cheaper, but the real value is not saving $11. It is the certainty that you will not get a larger bill at pickup.

5,500 locations include many Walmart Supercenters, which extends operating hours into evenings and weekends. For shift workers or parents who cannot take a weekday off, this matters. The Lifetime Accuracy Guarantee covers IRS or state penalties forever — not just for the current tax year. Customers report reaching chat support quickly even outside the filing season, when many storefront locations are closed.

Jackson Hewitt's preparers are not required to be CPAs or EAs. The training program is solid, but the average expertise level sits below what you get from a credentialed CPA firm. For W-2 earners with one or two additional schedules, that gap rarely matters. For a business owner with depreciation recapture, passive activity loss carryforwards, or an S-corp K-1, push the complexity question before you book.

sections.heading: TurboTax Live Full Service — best online expert experience
paragraphs: TurboTax Live Full Service assigns a credentialed expert — CPA or EA — who prepares and signs your return. You upload documents, answer questions via secure messaging, and schedule a video review call. For this scenario (Self-Employed tier) it is $469 federal plus $64 per state — $597 for two states. That is the highest price in this comparison by a significant margin.

Refund accuracy is where the price premium can pay for itself. Self-employed filers regularly report the expert review surfacing items they had missed — Section 179 equipment deductions and mileage-log discrepancies come up repeatedly — often enough to more than cover the fee difference. This is not a coincidence — Intuit routes complex returns to specialists matched by return type, and the matching system has improved considerably since 2024.

The tradeoff: you cannot walk into an office or call a local number. Everything is asynchronous until the video call, and self-employed filers report first-available appointments running several days out during the February peak. TurboTax Live also will not replace a CPA for ongoing business tax planning, entity structuring, or multi-year strategy. It is preparation, not advisory.

sections.heading: Local CPA or Enrolled Agent — best for genuinely complex returns
paragraphs: A Certified Public Accountant or IRS Enrolled Agent is the right call when your return involves an S-corp or partnership K-1, depreciation recapture, FBAR/FATCA foreign reporting, estate or trust income, or a year with multiple life events — sale of a business, divorce settlement, large stock option exercise. The national chains can handle moderate complexity. They are not equipped for edge cases.

For a scenario like this, local CPAs typically quote between $420 and $680. The real edge is elsewhere: a CPA catches items like a prior-year net operating loss carryforward that chain services routinely miss. Recover a carryforward like that once and the fee gap against a chain service disappears entirely. Year-round access matters too: a CPA can advise on Q4 estimated tax payments, retirement contribution timing, and Section 199A deduction optimization — value that is invisible at filing time.

Finding a good local CPA takes effort. Use the AICPA's CPA Locator (aicpa-cima.com) or the National Association of Enrolled Agents directory (naea.org). Ask specifically whether the preparer handles your return type regularly — a CPA who specializes in dental practices may not be fluent in real estate passive activity rules. Fees vary enormously by region: $300 in rural areas, $1,500+ in Manhattan for the same return. Get three quotes.

sections.heading: IRS VITA Program — best free option for qualifying filers
paragraphs: Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) is an IRS program that provides free tax preparation to households earning $67,000 or less. Volunteers complete a minimum of 15 hours of IRS-certified training and must pass certification exams before preparing any returns. The quality floor is higher than most people expect — IRS quality reviewers check every return before it is filed.

VITA sites operate from late January through April 15 at libraries, community centers, schools, and AARP locations. Many also offer Military OneSource extensions for service members. The 2026 network includes roughly 11,000 sites nationwide. Use the IRS VITA locator at irs.gov or call 1-800-906-9887 to find your nearest site and check what documents to bring.

VITA has real limits: volunteers cannot handle self-employment returns with expenses, rental income, or complex investment scenarios at most sites. Returns must meet the income threshold. There is no audit representation — if the IRS contacts you after filing, you handle that independently. For a W-2 earner with a standard deduction or basic itemized deductions and income under $67K, VITA delivers the same accuracy as a $200 professional service at no cost.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest legitimate way to file a complex return?
faqs.a: If your household income is under $67,000, VITA is free and IRS-certified — use that first. Above $67K with Schedule C or Schedule E, Jackson Hewitt's flat fee of $75–$250 is usually the lowest price among national chains, though TurboTax Live sometimes finds enough missed deductions to offset its higher cost.

faqs.q: Do I need a CPA or will H&R Block / TurboTax work?
faqs.a: H&R Block and TurboTax Live handle most individual returns well, including moderate self-employment and rental income. You likely need a CPA or EA if you have an S-corp or partnership K-1, foreign financial accounts (FBAR), depreciation recapture, or a major transaction like selling a business or exercising stock options.

faqs.q: Is TurboTax Live Full Service worth the price?
faqs.a: For self-employed filers and landlords, often yes — the credentialed experts frequently find deductions that justify the $469 Self-Employed tier. For simpler returns (W-2 plus one or two minor items), TurboTax Deluxe DIY at $59 covers you just as well.

faqs.q: What does 'audit support' actually mean at these services?
faqs.a: H&R Block's and TurboTax Live's audit support means a representative helps you respond to IRS correspondence and accompanies you to an audit without additional fees. Jackson Hewitt's Lifetime Accuracy Guarantee covers penalties and interest caused by preparer error, but does not provide in-person audit representation. VITA provides no audit support.

faqs.q: Can Jackson Hewitt handle self-employment income?
faqs.a: Yes. Jackson Hewitt preparers can file Schedule C returns, and the flat-fee structure means you pay the same whether your return is simple or includes business expenses. That said, for complex sole proprietors — particularly those with home office, vehicle, and depreciation deductions — ask the local office upfront whether their preparers handle Schedule C regularly.

faqs.q: How do I find a trustworthy local CPA?
faqs.a: Start with the AICPA CPA Locator at aicpa-cima.com or the NAEA enrolled agent directory at naea.org. Both verify active credentials. Ask any prospective preparer: what share of your clients have returns like this one, and do you handle any IRS correspondence that arises? Get quotes from at least three preparers.

faqs.q: What income level makes the VITA program inaccessible?
faqs.a: VITA covers households earning $67,000 or less for 2025 returns (filed in 2026). AARP Tax-Aide, a related program, has no income limit and is available to taxpayers of any age.

faqs.q: Can I switch from one service to another if I started already?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as you have not paid and the preparer has not filed. If you paid but the return is not yet filed, you can request a refund and start over — chains typically refund if filing has not occurred. If the return was already filed, you cannot undo that, but you can file an amended return (Form 1040-X) with a different preparer.

faqs.q: Does TurboTax Live Full Service include state returns?
faqs.a: Federal preparation is included in the tier price ($89 Basic through $469 Self-Employed). State returns cost an additional $64 per state. If you file in two states, add $128 to the quoted federal price.

faqs.q: What documents should I bring to an H&R Block or Jackson Hewitt appointment?
faqs.a: Bring all W-2s and 1099s, last year's return (for carry-forward items), Social Security numbers for yourself and dependents, mortgage interest statements (Form 1098), property tax records, health insurance documents (1095-A/B/C), and any receipts for deductions you plan to claim. Self-employed filers should also bring a profit/loss summary and mileage log.

offerNotes.hr-block-in-person-prep: 9,000 US offices, walk-in available, Accuracy Guarantee and audit representation included at no extra charge.
offerNotes.jackson-hewitt-tax-prep: Flat-fee pricing covers all schedules — no surprise add-ons. Lifetime Accuracy Guarantee covers penalties from preparer errors.
offerNotes.turbotax-live-full-service: Credentialed CPA or EA prepares and signs your return via video. Self-Employed tier at $469 plus $64/state.
offerNotes.local-cpa: Best for S-corp K-1s, FBAR, depreciation recapture, and year-round tax planning. Find credentialed preparers via AICPA or NAEA.
offerNotes.vita-program-free: Free IRS-certified filing for households under $67,000. Available January–April 15 at libraries and community centers nationwide.

pinDescription: TurboTax Live runs $597 for two states — here's when that still pays off.
